records.difference: Legacy source describes automatic deploy-time migration on npm build; canonical code explicitly requires CE_DB_MIGRATION_APPROVED=true, exactly --approved and rejects CI/GitHub Actions before connecting to DATABASE_URL.
records.required_next_evidence: Independent reviewer and negative tests for CI, absent CLI grant, absent DATABASE_URL and rollback in disposable PostgreSQL.

records.difference: Legacy enables authentication unless VITE_AUTH_ENABLED is exactly false and uses genericOAuthClient/signIn.oauth2; canonical requires explicit true and uses social sign-in. Blind replacement could re-enable auth or alter provider contract.
records.required_next_evidence: Browser and server tests of disabled/undefined/true flags and provider-specific OAuth flow, verified credentials and 401/403 negative cases.

records.difference: Canonical test has before/after hooks forcing positive auth scenario and restoring environment, unlike old version; historical copy would lose isolated positive coverage when CI sets VITE_AUTH_ENABLED=false.
records.required_next_evidence: Verify execution of negative auth-off and positive identity tests under CI, independently audit JWT issuer/audience and session binding.

records.difference: Source calls auth.api.signInWithOAuth2 with providerId; canonical calls auth.api.signInSocial with provider and disableRedirect=true. Functional equivalence depends on active provider plugins; no remote popup E2E performed.
records.required_next_evidence: Preview browser OAuth callback, cookie/bearer scope, redirect origin, token forwarding and error propagation tests; no real credentials exposed.

records.difference: Historical test assumes no SQL files in root migrations directory. Canonical test enumerates root SQL files and validates non-recursive auth isolation; historical assertion would regress once product migrations exist.
